content.title: What is a PSA Marriage Certificate?

blocks.content: A **PSA Marriage Certificate** is an official civil registry document issued by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) that serves as proof that a marriage has been legally registered in the Philippines.

blocks.content: The PSA-issued copy is the version most commonly required by government agencies and foreign embassies.

blocks.title: Is a Marriage Certificate the same as a Marriage Contract?

blocks.content: Yes. In the Philippines, people commonly use the terms interchangeably.

blocks.title: How long before a PSA Marriage Certificate becomes available?

blocks.content: Availability may take several weeks to several months after the wedding depending on local registry endorsement and PSA processing.
Yes. PSA-authorized online delivery services are available.

blocks.title: Can someone else request my certificate?

blocks.content: Yes, provided they have authorization documents and valid identification.

blocks.title: What happens if PSA has no record of my marriage?

blocks.content: You may need to coordinate with the Local Civil Registry Office where the marriage was registered for endorsement or correction.

blocks.title: Is the PSA digital e-certificate valid?

blocks.content: Yes. PSA digital e-certificates include verification systems and are legally recognized.
